purpose: close the deployment loop for a screen the group-safe certificate actually certifies: remove the frozen SCAn flags of the block-6 victims (all ten meet the all-class policy and receive GO), retrain from scratch, and compare attack success with size-matched random removal (internal review 2026-10-18, item 6)
development_disclosure: The block-6 victims, SCAn flags, and certificate decisions are known. No block-6 victim has been retrained after any removal. The design copies the frozen block-P post-filter protocol (seeds 202-211) and adds a size-matched random removal restricted to the SCAn-flagged classes as the primary control.
retraining: architecture, optimizer, epochs, batch size, loss, and validation-BCA checkpoint selection identical to the block-6 victim protocol; initialization seed = victim seed in every condition

analysis.primary_contrast: paired detector_scan minus random_matched_flagged attack success rate
analysis.support_rule: 95% percentile bootstrap upper bound of the paired ASR difference below zero and mean paired BCA difference at least -0.05

limitations: Hash-bound locally without a third-party timestamp.
One dataset, architecture, and attack (GTSRB global blend); the certificate and the retraining endpoint are separate claims.
